Policy rule R1: Verify before you block on a weak signal: R1. Verify before you block on a weak signal. Policy rule R6: Shared origin: R6. Shared origin. sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-29 and 2016-12-31, card C00782-K1 belonging to customer C00782 was used for 2 transaction(s) totalling $959.27, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $934.98 on 2016-12-29. The activity was conducted in person under product code W, billed in region 327.0, and on contact there was no reply within 24 hours, an assumption recorded in the case file because no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. 2 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on this transaction, and $934.98 is 12.7x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. The bank's closed investigations already record 1 confirmed fraud case(s) on this card (CC-3048), and the same device profile was used by 1 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-12-29 (C13355-K1), indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder. Connected components over the device-sharing graph place this card in a bounded component of 2 cards (C13355-K1), linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards, a component this small being a genuine shared origin rather than a common configuration. The activity is suspicious because it is consistent with mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number, and the bank has assessed the probability of this activity being fraudulent at 0.70 based on 2 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history, which also shows that 2 or more failed flags is 2.9x more likely on confirmed fraud than on a cleared alarm (22.7% vs 7.9%). The filing is made because the activity connects to a device profile shared with other compromised cards, and under Policy rule R6 when several cards show fraud from the same device profile the shared element must be named, a case must be created and a report filed, and every card that shares it must be monitored, which is why the cards sharing the same origin have been placed under monitoring. The total amount of suspicious activity is $959.27, the pending authorisation has been declined, the matter has been escalated to a fraud analyst, and an internal investigation case has been opened.
